Eh. The Pi is a pretty cool piece of hardware, but things add up. VPN endpoint and MC server take quite a bit of CPU. Nextcloud, as cited in the article, needs a httpd and that can be resource heavy. You'd need external cases/power for the HDs, and the PC wil likely already have enough power. I've also had HDs overheat in external cases. 5 year old PC will have 2-4 GB typically, and that beats the 1GB of the Pi. (PC takes a bit more overhead, but still gives more available.)

I built a NASberry Pi recently. It also pulls torrents of shows and movies that I want to watch without giving money to the jackasses that made them. Of course, if you want something faster than a Pi, I recommend Pine 64.

The Pi is ok for a single-user NAS, but as other comments pointed out, the Ethernet and USB are shared on a single pipe to the CPU, so throughput DOES suffer. I've found them to be somewhat better than the old Bifferboard NAS units (think those cheap ones you could buy 10-15 years ago) but not a whole lot. There are other options out there for single-board units that have a true SATA port, but they suffer from unreliability and poor community support.

I will say that the Pi is cheap enough that it's almost a hardware VM. I have three running side-by-side, each one doing a couple of independent tasks.
